reason: Rewrite R_{a,b,r}(q) as product_{i=a+1}^b (1-q^{r+i})/(1-q^i). Factoring each q^N-1 into cyclotomic polynomials shows that the exponent of Phi_d(q) is exactly the number of multiples of d in (r+a,r+b] minus the number of multiples of d in (a,b], namely M_d(r+a,r+b)-M_d(a,b). If some exponent were negative while the whole expression were a polynomial, then after clearing denominators and evaluating at a primitive d-th root of unity one gets a contradiction; hence all exponents are nonnegative.
